        El Paso Electric Coinpany (EPE) filed an application for approval of a new retail service
tariff, Schedule 27 - High Load Factor Large Power Service (HLFLP), under PURA § 36.003.
This preliminary order identifies the issues that must be addressed in this proceeding.

        EPE's proposed HLFLP tariff would set retail rates for electric service to very large data
center or advanced manufacturing customers in EPE's Texas service territory that have high annual
load factors. 1 To quali fy for service under the proposed tari ff, a customer must have an annual
peak demand of 75 megawatts (MW) or larger as well as an annual load factor of at least 85% and
must sign an energy service agreement (ESA) with EPE.2 The ESAs are to be developed on a
case-by-case basis using a standard form ESA attached to the proposed HLFLP tariff.3 EPE states
that it is not seeking review or approval of the ESA.4

        The high annual load factor and ESA requirements distinguish the proposed HLFLP tariff
from EPE's existing tariffs for large power service customers.5 However, the rates under the
proposed tariff are otherwise identical to the rates the Commission recently approved for EPE's
Schedule 33A - Large Economic Development Rate.6 Schedule 33A was designed by EPE for
use by Wurldwide LLC, a new data center that is estimated to initiate service in July 2026 and will

                                         I.   Procedural History
        EPE filed the application on April 7,2026. Motions to intervene filed by the following
were granted: Texas Industrial Energy Consumers (TIEC); the Office of Public Utility Counsel
(OPUC); the City of El Paso; New Horizon Devco, LLC; and Southwest Power Connection,
LLC.l 3 OPUC and the City of El Paso requested that this proceeding be referred to the State Office
of Administrative Hearings (SOAH) for a hearing on the merits.                      EPE was directed, and
Commission Staff and other interested persons were allowed, by June 22,2026 to file a list of
issues to be addressed in the docket and also identify any issues not to be addressed and any
threshold legal or policy issues that should be addressed. EPE filed a list of issues.

                                   II.     Issues to be Addressed
       The Commission must provide to the administrative law judge (ALJ) a list of issues or
areas to be addressed in any proceeding referred to SOAH.14 After reviewing the pleadings
submitted by the parties, the Commission identifies the following issues that must be addressed in
this docket:

1. Is this the appropriate proceeding for the relief sought by EPE? Should the Commission
    instead require any such relief to be sought in a base-rate proceeding or any other proceeding?

2. Is the application administratively complete?

3. Did EPE provide sufficient notice of the application?

4. Do the proposed rates, terms, and conditions for retail electric service for large-load,
   high-load-factor customers comply with the requirements of PURA § 36.003?
   a. Are the rates just and reasonable?

   b. Are the rates not unreasonably preferential, prejudicial, or discriminatory?

   c. Are the rates sufficient, equitable, and consistent in application to each class of consumer?

5. Is the proposed 20-year minimum initial term for service under proposed tariff HLFLP
   appropriate?

6. What tariffprovisions are subject to modification by mutual agreement by EPE and a customer
   taking service under the proposed HLFLP tariff based on the following sentence in the
   proposed tariff: "Unless otherwise mutually agreed to by the Company and the customer, the
   customer shall be billed under the provisions o f this tariff once the utility commences service
   consistent with the Energy Service Agreement, regardless of whether the customer has
   energized its facilities"?

7. What tariffprovisions are subject to the ESA's terms?

8. Is it appropriate for the ESA not to be subject to review or approval by the Commission?

9. What, if any, conditions should be placed on approval to ensure that Texas residential and
   small commercial customers are not unreasonably affected by approval of EPE's application?

   a. Should any dedicated incremental costs due to a customer that is being served under
       proposed tariff HLFLP be excluded from transmission cost recovery factor or generation
       cost recovery factor recovery~15

10. Is EPE requesting to recover rate-case expenses in this proceeding?

11. Does the proposed HLFLP tariff comply with all other applicable requirements of PURA and
   Commission rules?

       This list of issues is not intended to be exhaustive. The parties and the ALJ are free to raise
and address any issues relevant in this docket that they deem necessary, subject to any limitations
imposed by the ALJ or by the Commission in future orders issued in this docket. The Commission
may identify and provide to the ALJ in the future any additional issues or areas that must be
addressed, as permitted under Texas Government Code § 2003.049(e).


                              III.       Effect of Preliminary Order
       This Order is preliminary in nature and is entered without prejudice to any party expressing
views contrary to this Order before the SOAH ALJ at hearing. The SOAH ALJ, upon his or her
own motion or upon the motion of any party, may deviate from this Order when circumstances
dictate that it is reasonable to do so. Any ruling by the SOAH ALJ that deviates from this Order
may be appealed to the Commission. The Commission will not address whether this Order should
be modified except upon its own motion or the appeal of a SOAH ALJ's order. Furthermore, this
Order is not subject to motions for rehearing or reconsideration.
